title: Finite Symmetry Gauging as a Specified Model

items.title: Finite two-group lattice spin state-sum model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; dependency and source evidence is recorded in the batch notes and current readiness record.
items.statement:
A finite ordered simplicial complex $K$ has a finite vertex set with a total order and a collection of nonempty finite vertex subsets, called simplices, closed under taking nonempty subsets. Its dimension is the maximum of $|\sigma|-1$ over its simplices. A closed physical regulator is a finite ordered triangulation of a closed compact oriented smooth three-manifold; relative amplitudes are also defined on its finite ordered subcomplexes. The increasing vertex order orients every simplex.

Choose $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the trivial Abelian group $A=\{0\}$, the unique action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$, and the zero normalized Postnikov cocycle $\beta=0$. A background on $K$ is a flat edge cochain $a_{ij}\in G$, satisfying $a_{ij}+a_{jk}-a_{ik}=0$ on each ordered triangle; its face cochain $B$ is uniquely zero. A raw $1$-gauge arrow has vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and sends $a_{ij}$ to $a'_{ij}=g_i+a_{ij}-g_j$. The edge label $\lambda$ and vertex $2$-gauge label $t$ are necessarily zero, so this selected two-group is the ordinary finite $G$ symmetry regarded as a two-group with trivial $A$.

For each background $x=(a,0)$, the model's cell-value sets are $X_v=G$ at each vertex and a singleton at every positive-dimensional simplex. The configuration set is $\Phi_x=C^0(K;G)$, the set of spin assignments $\sigma=(\sigma_v)_{v\in K^{(0)}}$. There are no further constraints. Set the dimensionless action $S_x(\sigma)=0$, the finite measure weight $\mu_x(\sigma)=2^{-V_K}$, where $V_K$ is the number of vertices, and the observable algebra $\mathcal O_x=\operatorname{Fun}(\Phi_x,\mathbb C)$. A function is local when it depends on spins in a specified subcomplex. The local spin observable $m_v(\sigma)=(-1)^{\sigma_v}$ transforms nontrivially under the constant global $G$ action, so this $0$-form symmetry is effective. For a closed one-dimensional subcomplex $\gamma$, the product $\prod_{v\in\gamma^{(0)}}m_v(\sigma)$ is a line-supported observable defined without an attached surface. The selected $1$-form group is trivial: its only defect is $U_0(\Sigma)=1$, and the line observable has only the trivial $A$-character.

For a background gauge arrow with vertex labels $g$, the configuration bijection is $T_g(\sigma)_v=\sigma_v+g_v$ and the observable-algebra isomorphism is $\alpha_g(O)=O\circ T_g^{-1}$. These assignments respect identity and composition. The per-background partition weight is

$$
W_K(x)=Z_x=\sum_{\sigma\in\Phi_x}2^{-V_K}=1.
$$

The boundary state space on a subcomplex $L$ is the finite-dimensional space $\mathcal H(L)=\operatorname{Fun}(\pi_0\mathcal B(L),\mathbb C)$. For a fixed background $s$ on $L$, the relative convention fixes only this background restriction and sums over all spins on $K$ with weight $2^{-V_K}$; it does not fix boundary spin values. Thus the spin sector contributes $1$ for each extending background and introduces no additional seam factor. The relative background amplitude then uses the relative higher-gauge sum. All fields, action phases, measures, and amplitudes are dimensionless in the convention $\hbar=1$.

The closed-manifold data instantiate the finite-regulator two-group model interface. The relative subcomplex amplitudes and the background-only boundary state space are the additional boundary convention adopted here; they are not inferred from the closed-manifold interface. No continuum limit or empirical conclusion is part of this definition.

items.title: Adopted finite two-group gauging model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; dependency and source evidence is recorded in the batch notes and current readiness record.
items.statement: Adopt as the finite physical model the three-dimensional vertex-spin regulator with $G=\mathbb Z/2$, trivial $1$-form group $A=\{0\}$, zero Postnikov cocycle, zero action, and the normalized uniform measure on spins. Its global $G$ symmetry flips every spin, its background response is the unit weight for every flat background, and its selected boundary state space and relative amplitudes are those specified by the model definition. The finite background gauging and sewing prescription is part of this adopted model. This postulate says nothing about a continuum limit, an empirical realization, or the truth of any more general quantum field theory.

items.title: Gauge invariance and gluing in the finite symmetry model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; dependency and source evidence is recorded in the batch notes and current readiness record.
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite ordered oriented simplicial complex of dimension at most three in the relative extension of the selected model, with $V_K$ vertices and $E_K$ edges. For a closed physical regulator, $K$ is a finite ordered triangulation of a closed compact oriented smooth three-manifold. Use $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the trivial group $A=\{0\}$, the unique action $\rho$, the zero normalized Postnikov cocycle $\beta$, and the unit background response $W_K(x)=1$. The dynamical spin configurations for each background are $\Phi_x=C^0(K;G)$, with action $S_x=0$ and normalized measure $\mu_x(\sigma)=2^{-V_K}$. A background gauge arrow with vertex labels $g$ transports spins by $T_g(\sigma)=\sigma+g$ and transports observables by pullback.

For every background $x$, its spin partition weight is $Z_x=1$. The normalized background-gauging amplitude is
$$ Z_K^{(2)}=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(K)}\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}=\frac{1}{2^{V_K}}|\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)|. $$
For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed background $s$ on $L$, the relative background amplitude is
$$
Z_{K,L}^{(2)}(s)=2^{-(V_K-V_L)}|\{x\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K):x|_L=s\}|.
$$
If $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$ is a union of ordered subcomplexes with compatible restrictions and opposite induced seam orientations, the relative boundary amplitudes are gauge-invariant and obey
$$ Z_K^{(2)}=\sum_{[s]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(\Sigma)} Z_{K_2,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)Z_{K_1,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}. $$
For a one-vertex boundary complex the amplitude is $1/2$. These conclusions concern only the specified finite model; they do not establish a continuum quantum field theory or empirical behavior.

items.title: Point normalization in the finite symmetry model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; dependency and source evidence is recorded in the batch notes and current readiness record.
items.statement: Let $K$ consist of one vertex and no higher-dimensional simplices in the relative state-sum convention for the finite model with $G=\mathbb Z/2$ and $A=\{0\}$. There is one background object, its first automorphism group has order $2$, and its second automorphism group is trivial. The normalized spin partition weight for the unique background is $1$, and the normalized background-gauging amplitude is $1/2$.
items.physical_scope: One-vertex boundary evaluation in the adopted finite G = Z/2 model with trivial A and normalized spin measure; no continuum or empirical claim.
